data.name: Zadkiel
data.gender_notes: Zadkiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A priest or divine healer in ancient Israel. Translated as 'Righteousness of God' or 'Justice of God' in English. The name Zadkiel carries the meaning “Righteousness of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zadkiel usually hope their child will grow to embody righteousness of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Zadkiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Righteousness of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zadkiel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: צָדְקִיאֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַמַּלְאָךְ שֶׁהוּא צְדָקִים, צַדִּיקַת שֶׁל האל, שְׁמוֹ נִזְכָּר בְּתַעֲנוּת, בִּתְפִלָּה, וּבְתַשְׁבְחָה. הַשְּׁמוֹת שֶׁל הַמַּלְאָכִים, כּוֹבָעִים אֶת הַתְּמוּנָה שֶׁל אֱלֹהֵינוּ, וּמְדַבְּרִים עָלָיו. הַמַּלְאָךְ צָדְקִיֵל, צְדָקִים, הוּא סְמִיכָה, רַחֲמִים, וְצַדִּיק.

in_greek.name: Ζαδκιήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: ὄνομα τοῦ ἀγγέλου ὅς ἐστιν ὀρθοδόξος, πιστός, καὶ δικαιός. Ὁ ἀπόστολος Ἀνανίας ἔλαβε τὸ ὄνομα Ζαδκιήλ, ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ὅς ἔδωκε αὐτῷ τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην. Ὁ ἀγγέλος Ζαδκιήλ, ἔχει τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ μαρτυρῆσαι, σύνεσις, θαρρήσεως, καὶ δυνάμεως.

in_english.name: Zadkiel
in_english.meaning: name of the righteous angel Zadkiel
in_english.long_meaning: name of the angel who is righteous, faithful, and just. Zadkiel is the name of the angel who is a messenger of God, a helper, and a comforter. He is a guardian angel who watches over the righteous and protects them from harm. In the Bible, Zadkiel is mentioned as a name of the angel who is a witness and a messenger of God's will. The name Zadkiel is also associated with the qualities of justice, mercy, and righteousness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zadkiel holds significant cultural impact in Jewish and Christian traditions, symbolizing divine healing and priestly service. In Jewish scripture, Zadkiel is mentioned as one of the chief priests during the time of King David (1 Samuel 26:11) and is also remembered for his close friendship with King Darius I of Persia (Ezra 5:2), facilitating the restoration of Jerusalem's Second Temple. In Christian mysticism, Zadkiel is considered as an archangel associated with prayer, healing, and the stimulation of spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual meaning of the name Zadkiel represents a deep-rooted connection to divine healing, righteousness, and justice. Carrying this name signifies a calling to serve as a spiritual healer, channeling God's energy to bring about wholeness and restoration. With its historical connection to ancient priesthood, the name Zadkiel holds the sacred responsibility of both facilitating spiritual growth within oneself and sharing this wisdom and light with others, ultimately promoting unity and justice in the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zadkiel, meaning "Righteousness of God," represents the divine presence and guidance in times of spiritual distress. As an angel of purification, he inspires inner transformation and helps individuals connect with their higher selves.

biblical_reference.note: name of the angel who appears in Ezekiel and Daniel

historical_references.reference: In the apocryphal Book of Enoch, Zadkiel is mentioned as one of the seven archangels who stand before God and intervene in human affairs.
historical_references.context: The Book of Enoch is an ancient Jewish text, likely written between the 2nd century BC and the 1st century AD. It is not considered part of the biblical canon by most Jewish or Christian traditions, but it has influenced both.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, Zadkiel was identified with the biblical figure Sadakiel or Sedekiel, a priest who, according to the apocryphal Book of Ezra, supervised the rebuilding of the Second Temple in Jerusalem.
historical_references.context: During this time, there was a growing interest in the apocryphal texts, and various interpretations of these texts led to the identification of various figures, including Zadkiel, with biblical characters.
